entries.title: Markdown page fields
entries.body_md: - Added `ExtendedDatatype = Markdown` for page fields bound to a `Text` variable, `Text` table field, or `Text`-returning procedure, including bounded `Text`. entries.title: Bug fixes
entries.body_md:
- Fixed agentic AL LSP symbol searches returning an unexplained failure when requested while the workspace was still loading. The `al/symbolSearch` endpoint now waits briefly for initialization and otherwise returns guidance to retry after workspace loading completes.
- Word report layouts containing `INCLUDETEXT` or `INCLUDEPICTURE` field codes now produce a compiler warning.
- `al_symbolsearch` now finds top-level application objects by exact numeric object ID, including objects from dependency symbols.
- Fixed `al_symbolsearch` retaining fully materialized symbol descriptors for the active project and its dependencies after searches. Searches now traverse only the requested symbol scope and return additional results through continuation tokens.
- Fixed culture identification in extension translations, preserving distinct language variants and preventing duplicate-translation errors during publishing.
- Improved AL source formatting in Visual Studio Code and after BCal file writes and edits. Formatting now applies CodeCop-compatible operator, block, and control-keyword layout while keeping empty blocks and blocks with a single property compact. Set `al.legacyFormatting` to `true` to restore the previous formatting behavior in Visual Studio Code; BCal always uses the improved behavior.
- Fixed inconsistent event subscriber ordering when metadata-based event binding is enabled.
- Fixed AS0072, AS0073, AS0074, AS0075, and AS0076 being reported for unchanged obsolete members when a new extension object with a lower object ID targets the same object as an existing extension object.
- Fixed downloads of dependency symbols failing without retrying when another process temporarily locks the destination package. `altool listtests --force` still reports a locked cache-replacement failure instead of retrying.
- Fixed an issue where semantic token processing could crash when a preprocessor `#if` or `#elif` condition appeared inside a report data item, query data item, or XMLport table element.
- Fixed breakpoints in default interface method implementations not being hit when continuing execution with F5.
- Improved diagnostics for private NuGet symbol feeds. A feed that returns HTTP 401 now reports "requires authentication", while HTTP 403 reports "requires authentication or additional permissions" at the failed request, and any credentials embedded in a feed URL are stripped before the URL is written to logs.
- Fixed RoleCenter bookmarks created by Designer disappearing when their action targeted an invalid position in the Sections area. The bookmark is now placed in the default navigation location.
- Fixed generated reference previews omitting the `Subtype` and `TestHandlers` properties from test codeunits.
- Fixed Snapshot Debugging MCP snappoint input and decoded snapshot output being shifted by one line because internal zero-based positions were exposed instead of the one-based lines shown in Visual Studio Code.

entries.title: Snapshot debugging AL tests
entries.body_md:
- Added `run_tests` to the Snapshot Debugging MCP proxy so agents can execute selected AL tests in an isolated session attached to the armed snapshot, then collect the test capture through `stop_snapshot_debugging`.

entries.title: Share packaged resources between apps
entries.body_md:
Apps can now expose selected packaged resources to other apps. Add private resources to `resourceFolders` and shared resources to `publicResourceFolders` in `app.json`:

```json
{
  "resourceFolders": [
    ".resources"
  ],
  "publicResourceFolders": [
    ".publicResources"
  ]
}
```

Successful builds list every packaged public resource in both the ALC console and the Visual Studio Code output:

```text
Public resources included in the package (2):
  schemas/customer.json
  templates/invoice.txt
```

The existing `NavApp` overloads without an app ID continue to operate in the current app and can access both private and public resources:

```al
AllOwnResources := NavApp.ListResources();
PrivateConfiguration := NavApp.GetResourceAsJson('private-config.json');
```

The new app ID overloads cross the app boundary and can access only resources declared public by the provider:

```al
PublicResources := NavApp.ListResources(ProviderAppId, 'schemas/*.json');
CustomerSchema := NavApp.GetResourceAsJson(
    'schemas/customer.json',
    ProviderAppId,
    TextEncoding::UTF8);
```

Apps can also discover providers that expose a matching public resource and then enumerate each provider:

```al
ProviderAppIds := NavApp.ListAppsWithPublicResources('schemas/*.json');
foreach ProviderAppId in ProviderAppIds do begin
    PublicResources := NavApp.ListResources(ProviderAppId, 'schemas/*.json');
    foreach ResourceName in PublicResources do
        ProcessSchema(
            ProviderAppId,
            ResourceName,
            NavApp.GetResourceAsJson(ResourceName, ProviderAppId));
end;
```

`NavApp.ListResources()` returns the current app's combined private and public resources. `NavApp.ListResources(AppId)` is always public-only, even when `AppId` is the current app. Attempts to retrieve a private resource through an app ID return the same not-found error as a resource that does not exist.

entries.title: Query ReadState supports ReadCommitted
entries.body_md: AL queries can now use `ReadState = ReadCommitted` to read only committed data without guaranteeing that rows remain consistent throughout the transaction.

entries.title: Search symbols installed on the connected environment with `al_symbolsearch`
entries.body_md: The `al_symbolsearch` language model tool can now search the AL objects installed on the **connected Business Central environment**, not just your local project and downloaded symbols. Pass `filters.source = "environment"` to search the objects actually present on the tenant (Base App, System App, and installed apps / per-tenant extensions). Each match includes its **owning app** (`appId`, `appName`, `appPublisher`, `appVersion`) so an agent can add the missing `app.json` dependency and download that app's symbols before using the object. When a local (workspace) search finds nothing, the tool now hints that the object may be available on the connected environment.

entries.title: Agents in Business Central move to GPT-5.3-chat
entries.body_md:
From May through June, Agents in Business Central are upgrading to GPT-5.3-chat as the default model. This update rolls out gradually to environments across all regions.

**What's changing:**

- **New default model** — GPT-5.3-chat replaces the previous model, bringing improved quality and performance for agents in Business Central.
- **Model control for coded agents** — New methods when coding agents let you control model selection programmatically from AL.
- **Model visibility and selection in agent design experience** - Administrators can see which language model their agents use and select their preferred model from the available options in the agent configuration page.

**What to expect during rollout:**

The model update and the new UI for model selection roll out independently. Your environment might receive GPT-5.3-chat before the model selection UI and new methods become available. During this period, agents continue to work as expected with the new model.

Environments in the UK, India, and Australia will receive the update at a later date.

If you want to switch models for your *designed* agents after the selection UI becomes available, you can do so from the **Agents** page in Business Central. For coded agents, use the new model selection methods to control which model your agent uses. For those of you having started on the journey of designing and coding agents, then we highly recommend evaluating your agents again once the model has updated, as agent behavior, as well as accuracy, might be impacted.

entries.title: Audit how your app is reached across boundaries with `al graph`
entries.body_md:
The `al` command-line tool gains a new **`graph`** command group that helps you audit how the code in your apps is reachable across **accessibility and debuggability boundaries**. Build a static call graph across your extension and its dependencies, then ask questions such as: which of my **internal** APIs are reachable from a **public** surface, which public entry points expose a specific internal implementation, or what `[NonDebuggable]` code can be reached from the outside.

First build a graph from source (compiling the apps together so cross-app calls resolve):

```powershell
al graph extract-whole --corpus C:\src\MyApp --corpus C:\src\MyDependencies --out .\shards --graph .\g.jsonl
```

Then query it for the boundary you care about.

**How is my internal API reached from public entry points?** (internal ← public call transitions)

```powershell
al graph query --graph .\g.jsonl --from access:public --to "access:internal+app:<my-app-guid>" --paths
```

**What is the first public surface that exposes a specific internal target?** — the outermost entry points a caller could actually hit:

```powershell
al graph query --graph .\g.jsonl --to "obj:Codeunit/My Impl#DoSensitive" --frontier access:public
```

**What code that can't be inspected in the debugger is reachable from a public surface?**

`debuggable` is the single end-effect concept — can a method be stepped into in the AL debugger and have its parameters, locals, and return value inspected? A method is *not* debuggable (`!debuggable`) for any of three reasons: its app didn't opt into debugging (`resourceExposurePolicy.allowDebugging`, default `false`), the method is marked `[NonDebuggable]`, or it's a platform built-in. (Debuggability is independent of cloud/OnPrem scope.)

```powershell
al graph query --graph .\g.jsonl --from access:public --to "!debuggable+app:<my-app-guid>" --paths
```

**Where does non-debuggable code hand data to code you can debug?**

A secret handled inside non-debuggable code stays out of the debugger — until it crosses into a method you *can* step through, where its value (as a parameter or a return value) becomes inspectable. That crossing — code you can't inspect flowing into code you can — is expressed directly:

```powershell
al graph query --graph .\g.jsonl --from !debuggable --to debuggable --paths
```

For the *first* place execution becomes inspectable on each path (the nearest debuggable frontier), use `--frontier`:

```powershell
al graph query --graph .\g.jsonl --from !debuggable --frontier debuggable
```

Scope it to a single object to review one boundary at a time:

```powershell
al graph query --graph .\g.jsonl --from "obj:Codeunit/My Secret Handler+!debuggable" --to "obj:Codeunit/My Secret Handler+debuggable" --paths
```

Add `--format sarif` on `al graph export` to turn any such query into a clickable code-flow (see below).

Selectors combine with `,` (OR), `+` (AND) and `!` / `not:` (negate a single term) over primitives such as `access:`, `scope:`, `kind:`, `ns:`, `obj:`, `app:` — plus the named aliases `debuggable` (the end-effect above), `onprem-surface`, and `elevation`. `onprem-surface` is the OnPrem-gated boundary, broader than `scope:onprem` because it also covers OnPrem `Scope` tables (which compile under Cloud scope). Add `--exclude "ns:*Test*"` to drop test code. Use `al graph export --format dgml|graphml|sarif --from <selector> --to <selector>` to render any query as an interactive graph in Visual Studio or a clickable SARIF code-flow. Exported nodes carry their source location, so you can jump straight from the graph to the `.al` file — SARIF steps open at the exact line in Visual Studio or the VS Code SARIF viewer.

entries.title: IsolatedStorage.Get with read isolation level
entries.body_md:
`IsolatedStorage.Get` now accepts a read isolation level that controls how the key row is locked during the read. For example, `IsolationLevel::UpdLock` locks the row so it can be safely read, modified, and written back within the same transaction. This feature requires runtime version 18.0 or later.

```al
if IsolatedStorage.Get(Key, DataScope::Module, IsolationLevel::UpdLock, Value) then
    IsolatedStorage.Set(Key, NewValue, DataScope::Module);
```

entries.title: TestHandlers — lifecycle hooks for test codeunits
entries.body_md:
The new `TestHandlers` property on test codeunits lets you attach handler codeunits that receive callbacks at every stage of a test run. Use them for cross-cutting concerns such as logging, database cleanup, performance measurement, or custom test reporting — without modifying each test codeunit individually.

**Overview**

The feature introduces:

| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| `ITestHandler` interface | Defines six lifecycle callbacks that handler codeunits must implement. |
| `TestHandler` system enum (ID 2000000023) | Extensible registry where you map enum values to handler codeunit implementations. |
| `DefaultTestHandler` system enum (ID 2000000024) | Like `TestHandler`, but handlers registered here run automatically for **every** test codeunit without being listed in `TestHandlers`. |
| `TestHandlers` codeunit property | Comma-separated list of `TestHandler` enum value names. Only valid on codeunits with `Subtype = Test`. |
| `TestHandlerContext` type | Read-only context object passed to every callback with information about the running test. |

**Step 1 — Implement a handler codeunit**

Create a codeunit that implements `ITestHandler`. All six procedures have default (empty) implementations, so you only need to override the ones you care about:

```al
codeunit 50100 MyTestLogger implements ITestHandler
{
    procedure OnBeforeTestCodeunitRun(Context: TestHandlerContext)
    begin
        Message('Starting codeunit %1 (%2)', Context.CodeunitId, Context.CodeunitName);
    end;

    procedure OnAfterTestCodeunitRun(Context: TestHandlerContext)
    begin
        Message('Finished codeunit %1, Success = %2', Context.CodeunitId, Context.Success);
    end;

    procedure OnBeforeTestProcedureRun(Context: TestHandlerContext)
    begin
        Message('  Starting %1', Context.ProcedureName);
    end;

    procedure OnAfterTestProcedureRun(Context: TestHandlerContext)
    begin
        Message('  Finished %1, Success = %2', Context.ProcedureName, Context.Success);
    end;

    procedure OnBeforeTestCaseRun(Context: TestHandlerContext)
    begin
        Message('    Case %1', Context.TestCaseName);
    end;

    procedure OnAfterTestCaseRun(Context: TestHandlerContext)
    begin
        Message('    Case %1, Success = %2', Context.TestCaseName, Context.Success);
    end;
}
```

**Step 2 — Register the handler in the `TestHandler` enum**

Extend the system `TestHandler` enum and map a value to your implementation codeunit:

```al
enumextension 50100 MyTestHandlers extends TestHandler
{
    value(50100; MyLogger)
    {
        Implementation = ITestHandler = MyTestLogger;
    }
}
```

**Step 3 — Subscribe a test codeunit**

Set the `TestHandlers` property on any test codeunit. Multiple handlers are separated by commas and are invoked in the order listed:

```al
codeunit 50200 MyTests
{
    Subtype = Test;
    TestHandlers = MyLogger;

    [Test]
    procedure TestSomething()
    begin
        // ...
    end;
}
```

**Default handlers**

To run a handler for *all* test codeunits automatically (without listing it in every `TestHandlers` property), extend `DefaultTestHandler` instead:

```al
enumextension 50101 MyDefaultHandlers extends DefaultTestHandler
{
    value(50101; GlobalLogger)
    {
        Implementation = ITestHandler = MyGlobalLogger;
    }
}
```

Default handlers run before any codeunit-specific handlers.

**Callback invocation order**

For a test codeunit with two test procedures where the second uses `[TestDataSource]` with two cases, and one handler registered, the callbacks fire in this order:

```
OnBeforeTestCodeunitRun          — once, before any procedure
  OnBeforeTestProcedureRun       — before procedure 1
  OnAfterTestProcedureRun        — after procedure 1
  OnBeforeTestProcedureRun       — before procedure 2
    OnBeforeTestCaseRun          — before case A of procedure 2
    OnAfterTestCaseRun           — after case A of procedure 2
    OnBeforeTestCaseRun          — before case B of procedure 2
    OnAfterTestCaseRun           — after case B of procedure 2
  OnAfterTestProcedureRun        — after procedure 2
OnAfterTestCodeunitRun           — once, after all procedures
```

`OnBeforeTestCaseRun` / `OnAfterTestCaseRun` are only invoked for procedures that use the `[TestDataSource]` attribute for data-driven testing.

**`TestHandlerContext` members**

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CodeunitId` | `Integer` | The ID of the test codeunit being run. Always populated. |
| `CodeunitName` | `Text` | The fully qualified name of the test codeunit. Always populated. |
| `ProcedureName` | `Text` | The name of the test procedure. Empty in codeunit-level callbacks (`OnBeforeTestCodeunitRun`, `OnAfterTestCodeunitRun`). |
| `Success` | `Boolean` | Whether the test completed successfully. Only meaningful in `OnAfter*` callbacks; always `false` in `OnBefore*` callbacks. |
| `TestCaseName` | `Text` | The name of the data-driven test case. Only populated in `OnBeforeTestCaseRun` and `OnAfterTestCaseRun`. |

entries.title: Translations with namespaces
entries.body_md:
We have added a new compiler feature flag, `TranslationsWithNamespaces`, that includes the object's namespace in translation IDs to avoid collisions between objects with the same name. When enabled, the translation ID format also changes so the object and property names are visible.
If a readable translation ID would contain non-ASCII characters, the compiler now uses the hashed format so generated translation IDs remain ASCII-only.
The new Ids:
`Namespace AL.ExampleNamespace - Page SamplePage - Property Caption`

The previous Ids:
`Page 1066360047 - Property 2879900210`

entries.title: Improvements to Agentic development
entries.body_md: - New AL0926 diagnostic to help coding agents (and developers) that have unintentionally mixed up the order of sections in an object by, for example, putting the `fieldgroups` section before the `keys` section on a table object. The current diagnostics for this case are an AL0104 ('}' expected) and an AL0198 (Expected one of the application object keywords) in combination, which might not give full transparency into solving the issue.

entries.title: Bug fixes
entries.body_md:
- Fixed Snapshot Debugging MCP snappoint input and decoded snapshot output being shifted by one line because internal zero-based positions were exposed instead of the one-based lines shown in Visual Studio Code.
- Fixed breakpoints in default interface method implementations not being hit when continuing execution with F5.
- Fixed AL0886 being reported from runtime 18 when a table extension key references a field added by a table extension that is packaged in the same app as the base table.
- AL report layout and analysis view file path properties (`RDLCLayout`, `WordLayout`, `ExcelLayout`, `LayoutFile`, and `DefinitionFile`) now accept both `/` and `\` directory separators on all operating systems, so the same AL source compiles identically on Windows and Linux. AL0363 ("The directory separator used in this property value is not compatible with the current operating system.") is no longer reported; the diagnostic ID is reserved for backwards-compatible suppression syntax.
- Fixed an issue where a `case` statement over a `Time` variable with `Time` literal labels would cause the compiler to emit invalid C# (`case NavTime.Create(...):`) that fails with CS0426. The compiler now correctly emits an `if`/`else` chain for `Time` literals, consistent with the existing behavior for `Date` and `Decimal`.
- Fixed an issue where certain AppSourceCop upgrade rules would crash with `AD0001` when a table or tableextension defines two keys with the same name.
- Fixed an issue where publishing an extension would launch the browser even when publishing failed.
- Fixed the agent extension template so that toggling the agent's **State** inside the embedded Agent Setup Part correctly enables the **Update** action on the parent setup page, unblocking activation.
- Fixed an issue where AL sources declaring `dotnet { assembly(mscorlib) }` or referencing BCL types such as `DotNet System.Int64` failed on Linux (and other CoreCLR hosts) with `AL0451: An assembly named 'System.Private.CoreLib' could not be found`, even when the .NET runtime directory was supplied via `-assemblyprobingpaths`. The default `AssemblyLocator` now resolves BCL assemblies that ship with the running .NET runtime, and the compatibility check no longer filters out .NET 10 composite ReadyToRun BCL DLLs.
- Fixed an issue where the "Add namespace" code action for CodeCop rule [AA0247](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/analyzers/codecop-aa0247) was not offered when none of the resolution strategies worked. Strategies using the `$(parentfolder)` placeholder, the publisher name, or project name are now normalized into a valid namespace, and the action falls back to `Default.Namespace` when no valid name can be derived, so the action is always available.
- Fixed CodeCop rules AA0181 and AA0233 handling for explicit `Find` search modes. `Find('-')` and `Find('+')` are recognized as dataset operations, while `Find('=')` and `Find('<>')` remain single-record operations.
- CodeLens element for code coverage now uses the user-selected default run profile when running the related tests.
- Fixed an issue where an enum value or option member used as a field's `InitValue` was not detected by **Find All References** and was not updated when renaming that enum value or option member.
- Fixed a compiler issue where pages with user-defined GetDecimalString methods could result in C# compilation errors.
- Fixed an issue where the generated AL table proxies for CDS/Dataverse integration referenced base tables by their bare short name. When two referenced apps defined a table with the same name (for example `FS Customer Asset` in both the Base Application and Field Service Integration), the reference was ambiguous and the compile failed with AL0275. Generated `extends`, `TableRelation`, and `CalcFormula` references are now fully namespace-qualified.
- Added the `IsDirty` property to the Record API.
- Applied additional validation and filtering when loading rule sets from external `http`/`https` URLs.
- [#8289](https://github.com/microsoft/AL/issues/8289) Fixed an issue where the AL Language extension entered a perpetual "Loading workspace" state when opening a multi-root workspace whose folder roots contained no `app.json` (for example, a documentation folder combined with a folder whose AL projects live only in nested subfolders). The client now skips the progress notification when no AL workspace folder can be activated, and the language server completes the progress explicitly when the active-workspace request is not backed by a manifest.
- Fixed an issue where a multi-project workspace would not load all dependencies.

entries.title: ALTool changes
entries.body_md:
- Added `runtests` command to run AL test codeunits directly from the command line without the MCP server, enabling CI/CD test automation scenarios.
- `runtests` now emits structured, machine-parseable JSON on stdout by default (pass/fail/skip counts and per-method results), keeping stdout free of log noise; pass `--raw` for the previous human-readable console output.
- Cloud targets continue to use AAD/OAuth by default. For headless on-premises and container scenarios, `publishapp` and `runtests` now read missing connection values from `BC_SERVER_URL`, `BC_SERVER_INSTANCE`, and `BC_SERVER_PORT`; when `BC_SERVER_USERNAME` and `BC_SERVER_PASSWORD` are also set, UserPassword authentication is selected automatically. Explicit command-line options and cloud targets continue to take precedence.
- Added `--noauth` support to `al LaunchMcpServer` so headless MCP scenarios can bypass server-side auth prompting while still using the configured connection details for publish, test, and symbol operations.
- Added `al launchlspserver`, a standard LSP server over stdio that any LSP-capable AI agent or editor can consume for full AL language intelligence (completions, hover, go-to-definition, find references, rename, formatting, inlay hints, etc.). Distributed as part of the [AL dotnet tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-tool-package) nuget package; see [AL Language Server for agentic development](#al-language-server-for-agentic-development-al-launchlspserver) below for usage.
- Added `altool launchprofilingmcpproxy`, a stdio MCP proxy that connects an AI agent to a Business Central server's Performance Profiling MCP context to capture `.alcpuprofile` CPU profiles from a slow session; the target session id is supplied per tool call. See [Performance Profiling MCP](#performance-profiling-mcp-capture-cpu-profiles-from-a-running-session) below for usage.
- Added `altool launchsnapshotmcpproxy`, a stdio MCP proxy that connects an AI agent to a Business Central server's Snapshot Debugging MCP context to capture an AL snapshot from the next session that reproduces a failing scenario — no debugging session or up-front session id required. See [Snapshot Debugging MCP](#snapshot-debugging-mcp-capture-al-snapshots-from-a-running-session) below for usage.
- Added `--errorlogdirectory` to `altool workspace compile`. When set, each project emits a structured error log (`<project>_<timestamp>.errorLog.json`) into the specified directory, enabling AL code-analysis alert tracking for the workspace-compilation build path. When omitted, no error logs are written.
- `runtests` can now execute a batch of codeunits over a single connection via `--testgroups <file>`, a JSON file of `[{ "codeunitId": 134001, "testMethods": ["MethodA"] }, ...]` where each group pairs a codeunit with the methods to run in it (an empty or omitted `testMethods` runs all of that codeunit's methods). The whole batch runs with one authentication and one server session, avoiding the per-codeunit connect cost of invoking `runtests` once per codeunit. `--testgroups` cannot be combined with the `codeunitId` argument or `--testmethods`.

entries.title: Removed al.editorServicesPath configuration property
entries.body_md: The `al.editorServicesPath` configuration property has been removed. The extension now always uses the standard `bin/` folder for all binaries. If you have this property configured in your settings, you should remove it as it will no longer have any effect.

entries.title: Automatic .NET runtime acquisition
entries.body_md:
The AL Language extension now uses automatic .NET runtime acquisition through the [.NET Install Tool for VS Code](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.vscode-dotnet-runtime). When the extension starts, it automatically downloads and installs the required .NET 10.0 runtime if it's not already present on your system.

Private marketplace environments must make the .NET Install Tool available so VS Code can install the AL Language extension dependency. If runtime acquisition fails after activation, AL Language falls back to a compatible ASP.NET Core runtime already installed through the system `dotnet` command.

This change significantly reduces the extension size by eliminating platform-specific runtime copies for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

entries.title: Code analyzers now deployed in bin folder
entries.body_md:
Code analyzers (CodeCop, AppSourceCop, UICop, PerTenantExtensionCop) are now deployed directly in the `bin/` folder alongside other extension binaries, avoiding duplication. Previously, analyzers were in a separate `bin/Analyzers` subfolder.

The unused `al.editorServicesPath` configuration property has been removed as the extension now always uses the standard `bin/` folder for all binaries.

entries.title: Visual Studio Code authentication is now enabled by default
entries.body_md:
The `useVsCodeAuthentication` setting now defaults to `true`. Authentication tokens are acquired through Visual Studio Code's built-in authentication instead of the extension's interactive or device code login.

This applies to all debug configurations (`launch` and `attach`) and the `al.useVsCodeAuthentication` workspace setting. If you need to use the legacy interactive or device code login, set `useVsCodeAuthentication` to `false` in your `launch.json` or workspace settings.

entries.title: Restrict global symbol downloads to a specific minor version
entries.body_md:
The new `al.globalSourcesEnforceMinorVersion` setting controls how the AL extension resolves package versions when downloading symbols from global sources.

By default (`false`), the extension downloads the latest available version within the same major version as specified in `app.json`. When set to `true`, resolution is restricted to versions matching both the major and minor version, downloading the highest available patch within that minor. This applies to both direct dependencies and propagated dependencies.

```json
"al.globalSourcesEnforceMinorVersion": true
```

entries.title: MCP Server: Add projects at runtime with `al_addproject`
entries.body_md:
The `--projects` parameter for `al LaunchMcpServer` is now optional. The server can start without any projects loaded and projects can be added dynamically at runtime using the new `al_addproject` tool.

```bash
al LaunchMcpServer --port 5000
```

Once the server is running, agents can call `al_addproject` with the path to an AL project folder (containing an `app.json` file) to load it into the workspace. All other tools (`al_compile`, `al_build`, `al_symbolsearch`, etc.) will return an actionable error if invoked before any projects have been added.

entries.title: MCP Server: File logging support
entries.body_md:
The MCP server now supports file-based logging for diagnostics and troubleshooting. Use the `--logfile` and `--loglevel` arguments to enable logging:

```bash
al LaunchMcpServer --port 5000 --logfile C:\logs\almcp.log --loglevel Verbose
```

Available log levels are `Debug`, `Verbose`, `Normal`, `Warning`, and `Error`. Use `--nolog` to disable logging entirely. If `--logfile` is not specified, logging defaults to `~/.al-mcp/almcp.log` (portable across Windows, Linux, and macOS).

entries.title: Allocate free AL object IDs with `al_getnextobjectid`
entries.body_md:
A new tool, `al_getnextobjectid`, is now available across the three agent-facing surfaces — Visual Studio Code's Language Model tools (Copilot Chat), the AL MCP server (`al LaunchMcpServer`), and the AL LSP server (`al launchlspserver`). Agents can call it during scaffolding to allocate free object IDs for any application object (Table, Page, Codeunit, Report, Query, XmlPort, Enum, PermissionSet, and the matching `*Extension` types) without having to read `app.json` themselves or risk colliding with existing objects in the project.

Inputs:

- `objectType` (required) — e.g. `"Codeunit"`, `"PageExtension"`. The tool's error message lists every supported value if an unknown type is passed.
- `count` (optional, default `1`, max `50`) — return up to N free IDs in one call.
- `rangeStart` / `rangeEnd` (optional) — narrow allocation to an explicit range; the range is intersected with the project's `idRanges` from `app.json`. When omitted, the project's manifest ranges are used in full.

The result includes the allocated IDs, the resolved ranges, and an `outOfRange` indicator (with the next ID past the configured ranges) when fewer IDs were available than requested. The scan is syntax-only and project-scoped — IDs declared in installed app dependencies or other extensions published to the same dev sandbox are not considered, so the tool always emits an advisory warning describing this limitation.

entries.title: Performance Profiling MCP: capture CPU profiles from a running session
entries.body_md:
A new Performance Profiling MCP surface lets an AI agent capture `.alcpuprofile` CPU profiles from a slow Business Central session and analyze the hot AL code paths. Unlike the troubleshooting MCP — which targets the session you are actively debugging — profiling is a standalone scenario: the target session id is supplied per tool call (the agent reads it from the prompt, e.g. *"why is session 10 slow?"*), so no debugging session is required.

**Command line (`altool launchprofilingmcpproxy`)**

The [AL dotnet tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-tool-package) now includes a `launchprofilingmcpproxy` command — a stdio MCP server that forwards an agent's profiling tool calls (`schedule_profiling`, `stop_schedule_and_get_profiles`, `get_profile_for_activity`) to a Business Central server's Profiling MCP context. The connection is configured once from launch.json-style parameters; the target session id is a per-call tool argument.

```bash
# On-premises
altool launchprofilingmcpproxy --environmenttype OnPrem --server http://localhost --serverinstance BC --port 7047 --authentication UserPassword

# Cloud (sandbox)
altool launchprofilingmcpproxy --environmenttype Sandbox --environmentname sandbox --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
```

Credentials come from the environment and are never stored in the configuration. For **cloud** connections the proxy authenticates non-interactively (it never opens a browser) and resolves a token in this order: (1) the `BC_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable — in Visual Studio Code agent mode the extension injects your VS Code sign-in token here automatically, and for headless/CI hosts you set it yourself; (2) a token cached by a prior interactive `altool auth login`. For **on-premises** hosts, `BC_SERVER_USERNAME`/`BC_SERVER_PASSWORD` supply `UserPassword` (Basic) authentication, and `Windows` authentication uses the current Windows identity with no credentials. For a multitenant on-premises server, pass `--tenant` to target a specific tenant. The same `--logfile`, `--loglevel`, and `--nolog` diagnostics as the other commands are supported.

**Visual Studio Code (agent mode)**

The extension now registers a **Business Central Profiling MCP Server** as an MCP server definition provider, so GitHub Copilot agent mode can profile a session directly — with no manual `mcp.json` setup. The connection is derived from the active AL project's launch.json (cloud environment/tenant or on-premises server/instance), and authentication reuses your Visual Studio Code sign-in. Ask the agent a question that names the slow session (for example, *"Business Central is slow for session 10, can you find out why?"*) and it starts the capture, asks you to reproduce the slow scenario, stops, and analyzes the resulting profile.

**Delivery of the captured profiles**

The proxy serves the captured schedule archive over MCP `resources/read` (it advertises the `resources` capability) and also writes each captured `.alcpuprofile` / archive to a local profile folder, returning the file path in the tool result — so MCP hosts that do not surface embedded binary resource content (such as the GitHub Copilot CLI) can still read the profile from disk. Auto-captured profiles are grouped in per-schedule subfolders under a dedicated `schedules` folder, and removed once past a retention window (1 day by default, configurable with `--profileretentiondays`); cleanup is call-driven (proxy startup and the next capture), not a background timer. The profile folder location is configurable with `--profilefolder` (default `%TEMP%/bc-profiling`). A new **`analyze_profiles_in_folder`** tool analyzes profiles you place in the `user` subfolder — which the proxy never auto-deletes — for profiles obtained out of band. These local files can contain sensitive business data, so handle them securely and in line with your privacy requirements.

**Session memory usage**

Alongside the CPU samples, each captured `.alcpuprofile` now carries the profiled session's estimated total managed memory and object count, and the agent presents them in a human-readable form so you can see at a glance whether memory is a factor. This is on by default, with nothing extra to turn on.

**Recovering the target session from a schedule id**

`stop_schedule_and_get_profiles` and `get_profile_for_activity` no longer require `targetSessionId` when the agent passes a `scheduleId` armed by an earlier `schedule_profiling` call in the same session — the proxy remembers which session each schedule was armed on and routes the call automatically. `targetSessionId` remains accepted and takes precedence when supplied.

entries.title: Snapshot Debugging MCP: capture AL snapshots from a running session
entries.body_md:
A new Snapshot Debugging MCP surface lets an AI agent capture an AL snapshot from a Business Central session that reproduces a failing scenario and then debug the recorded execution offline. Snapshot debugging *arms* the server and records the **next** session that reproduces the problem: the agent initializes a debugging context (optionally scoped to a specific user), you reproduce the scenario, and the agent stops and collects the snapshot. There is often no target session yet, so a session id isn't required up front; if you already have a running session in mind, its id can be supplied to attach to that session directly.

**Command line (`altool launchsnapshotmcpproxy`)**

The [AL dotnet tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-tool-package) now includes a `launchsnapshotmcpproxy` command — a stdio MCP server that forwards an agent's snapshot tool calls (`initialize_snapshot_debugging`, `stop_snapshot_debugging`, `get_snapshot_status`) to a Business Central server's Snapshot Debugging MCP context. The connection is configured once from launch.json-style parameters.

```bash
# On-premises
altool launchsnapshotmcpproxy --environmenttype OnPrem --server http://localhost --serverinstance BC --port 7047 --authentication UserPassword

# Cloud (sandbox)
altool launchsnapshotmcpproxy --environmenttype Sandbox --environmentname sandbox --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
```

Credentials come from the environment and are never stored in the configuration. For **cloud** connections the proxy authenticates non-interactively (it never opens a browser) and resolves a token in this order: (1) the `BC_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable — in Visual Studio Code agent mode the extension injects your VS Code sign-in token here automatically, and for headless/CI hosts you set it yourself; (2) a token cached by a prior interactive `altool auth login`. For **on-premises** hosts, `BC_SERVER_USERNAME`/`BC_SERVER_PASSWORD` supply `UserPassword` (Basic) authentication, and `Windows` authentication uses the current Windows identity with no credentials. For a multitenant on-premises server, pass `--tenant` to target a specific tenant. The same `--logfile`, `--loglevel`, and `--nolog` diagnostics as the other commands are supported.

**Visual Studio Code (agent mode)**

The extension now registers a **Business Central Snapshot MCP Server** as an MCP server definition provider, so GitHub Copilot agent mode can capture a snapshot directly — with no manual `mcp.json` setup. The connection is derived from the active AL project's launch.json (cloud environment/tenant or on-premises server/instance), and authentication reuses your Visual Studio Code sign-in. Ask the agent to investigate a failing scenario (for example, *"a user hits an error posting a sales order — capture a snapshot so we can debug it"*); it initializes the context, asks you to reproduce the scenario, then stops and returns the recorded snapshot.

**Delivery of the captured snapshot**

`stop_snapshot_debugging` returns the recorded snapshot archive either inline (a base64-encoded `.zip`) or, for larger captures, as an MCP `resources/read` `resourceUri` the proxy serves on demand — so MCP hosts that do not surface embedded binary resource content can still read the archive by its URI. The archive can contain sensitive business data, so handle it securely and in line with your privacy requirements.

**Environment moves and restarts**

A snapshot that is still being captured may not survive the environment being moved or restarted. If that happens, `get_snapshot_status` reports the context as not found — just initialize a new snapshot and reproduce the scenario again.

entries.title: AL Language Server for agentic development (`al launchlspserver`)
entries.body_md:
The [AL dotnet tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-tool-package) now includes a new `launchlspserver` command. This starts a standard [Language Server Protocol (LSP)](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) server over stdio, allowing AI agents and editors that speak LSP to get full AL language intelligence without requiring a Visual Studio Code client.

```bash
al launchlspserver --projects "C:\Users\MyUser\MyALProject"
```

Once running, the server responds to standard LSP requests including completions, hover, go-to-definition, find references, document symbols, rename, formatting, inlay hints, folding ranges, and type hierarchy. Projects and per-project options can also be supplied at runtime via the LSP `initialize` request's `initializationOptions`.

Per-workspace configuration can additionally be sourced from a `<rootUri>/.vscode/settings.json` — the same file the AL Visual Studio Code extension reads. Recognized `al.*` keys (`packageCachePath`, `assemblyProbingPaths`, `ruleSetPath`, `enableCodeAnalysis`, `codeAnalyzers`) override CLI defaults at startup, and LSP `initializationOptions` from the client take final precedence. JSONC comments and trailing commas are tolerated. Use `--settingspath` to point at a specific settings.json (any Visual Studio Code scope — user, workspace, or folder) when the LSP host doesn't pass the workspace's actual `rootUri`, or when one user account works across multiple AL workspaces.

For multi-app workspaces, `--workspacefile` accepts a Visual Studio Code `.code-workspace` file directly: its `folders` populate the projects loaded at startup and its inline `settings` block contributes the same `al.*` keys. This lets a single file drive both project layout and configuration, matching how Visual Studio Code itself opens the workspace.

The command supports the same compilation and logging options as `launchmcpserver`:

```
  [projects]                Optional. AL project paths to load at startup.

  --packagecachepath        Paths to the package cache folders.

  --assemblyprobingpaths    Paths to probe for dependent assemblies.

  --ruleset                 Path to the ruleset file.

  --outfolder               Output folder for compilation artifacts.

  --codeanalyzers           Code analyzers to enable.

  --settingspath            Optional. Path to a settings.json (any VS Code scope
                            — user, workspace, or folder) whose al.* keys
                            override CLI defaults at startup. When omitted,
                            auto-discovered from the initialize request's
                            rootUri (walking ancestors).

  --workspacefile           Optional. Path to a VS Code .code-workspace file. Its
                            `folders` extend the projects loaded at startup
                            (merged with the positional projects argument), and
                            its inline `settings` block contributes al.* keys
                            as workspace-level config. --settingspath, when also
                            supplied, overrides the inline settings.

  --logfile                 Path to the log file. Defaults to ~/.al-mcp/almcp.log.

  --loglevel                Log level: Debug, Verbose, Normal (default), Warning, Error.

  --nolog                   Disable logging entirely.

  --disableTelemetry        Disable telemetry collection.
```

To use the AL Language Server with Claude Code or another LSP-capable AI agent, configure the server as an LSP plugin pointing to `altool launchlspserver`. See the [Claude Code plugin documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins) for how to create a plugin, and the [LSP server reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers) for the full `.lsp.json` schema.

entries.title: Default interface method implementations
New properties on ModuleInfo
entries.body_md:
The `ModuleInfo` type now exposes additional app manifest metadata. These properties require runtime version 18.0 or later:

- `Help` — Returns the help link of the specified application.
- `EULA` — Returns the End User License Agreement (EULA) link of the specified application.
- `PrivacyStatement` — Returns the privacy statement link of the specified application.
- `ContextSensitiveHelpUrl` — Returns the context sensitive help URL with the user's locale resolved from the application's supported locales.

```al
procedure ShowAppMetadata()
var
    appInfo: ModuleInfo;
begin
    NavApp.GetCurrentModuleInfo(appInfo);
    Message('Help: %1\EULA: %2', appInfo.Help, appInfo.EULA);
end;
```

entries.title: Data-driven tests
entries.body_md:
When writing tests, you can now create data-driven tests by using the `TestDataSource` attribute. It has two arguments: the codeunit that generates the test cases and a text literal for the dataset identifier. The test method must take exactly one parameter of type `interface ITestContext` (or an interface that extends it).

```AL
[TestDataSource(Codeunit::"Late Fee Test Data Source", 'LateFeeTestData.json')]
procedure LateFeeTest(Context: interface "ILate Fee Test Context")
begin
    VerifyLateFee(Context);
end;
```

The referenced codeunit must implement the `ITestDataSource` interface. This interface has a single function, `GetDataRows`, where the first argument is the text literal from the `TestDataSource` attribute. The second argument is a type that provides context about the test codeunit. Each item in the returned list is a test case.
```AL
procedure GetDataRows(DataSetIdentifier: Text; context: DataSourceContext): List of [interface ITestContext]
begin
end;
```

Each test case is based on the `ITestContext` interface, which has a single function that returns the identifier of the test case. This identifier must be deterministic and remain the same for each run of the test function.
```AL
interface ITestContext
{
    procedure Identifier(): Text;
}
```

entries.title: Support for BigInteger field migration
entries.body_md:
The compiler now supports gradual migration between Integer and BigInteger field types:

**1. Field type changes (Integer → BigInteger)**: Changing an existing table field from Integer to BigInteger is now supported when targeting runtime version 18.0 (Fall 2026) or later. A new AppSourceCop rule (AS0141) warns about the potential consequences for dependent extensions that reference the field.

**2. Property context warnings**: When referencing a BigInteger field in property contexts (TableRelation, CalcFormula WHERE clauses, etc.), the compiler emits warnings for narrowing conversions (BigInteger → Integer) to alert about potential overflow at runtime.

Key behaviors:

- **Field upgrades**: Integer → BigInteger changes are allowed in upgrade scenarios
- **Property warnings**: BigInteger → Integer,Option,Enum conversions in WHERE clauses emit warnings about potential overflow
- **CalcFormula support**: LOOKUP, MAX, and MIN operations allow Integer ↔ BigInteger conversions with appropriate warnings for narrowing conversions

entries.title: Agents in Business Central move to GPT-5.3-chat
entries.body_md:
From May through June, Agents in Business Central are upgrading to GPT-5.3-chat as the default model. This update rolls out gradually to environments across all regions.

**What's changing:**

- **New default model** — GPT-5.3-chat replaces the previous model, bringing improved quality and performance for agents in Business Central.
- **Model control for coded agents** — New methods when coding agents let you control model selection programmatically from AL.
- **Model visibility and selection in agent design experience** - Administrators can see which language model their agents use and select their preferred model from the available options in the agent configuration page.

**What to expect during rollout:**

The model update and the new UI for model selection roll out independently. Your environment might receive GPT-5.3-chat before the model selection UI and new methods become available. During this period, agents continue to work as expected with the new model.

Environments in the UK, India, and Australia will receive the update at a later date.

If you want to switch models for your *designed* agents after the selection UI becomes available, you can do so from the **Agents** page in Business Central. For coded agents, use the new model selection methods to control which model your agent uses. For those of you having started on the journey of designing and coding agents, then we highly recommend evaluating your agents again once the model has updated, as agent behavior, as well as accuracy, might be impacted.

entries.title: New warning AL0914: Excel layout contains an orphaned sheet after automatic multi-sheet upgrade

However, the original template sheet (typically named `Data`) is left in the workbook as an orphan; the rendered report will contain this orphaned sheet, which may confuse end users. To resolve the warning, delete the layout file and let the compiler regenerate it cleanly.

entries.title: Run tests from Visual Studio Code
entries.body_md:
It is now possible to use the VSCode Test Explorer to run tests. Running tests is only supported on Business Central version 28.0 and newer, on both sandboxes and local servers.

We support the following run profiles:
- **Publish & Run**: Publishes the test project and any of its dependencies before running the selected tests.
- **Run**: Runs all selected tests without pre-publishing the test project. If what is published on the server is out of sync with what is in VSCode, some tests may not get executed.
- **Run & Debug**: Starts a debugging session and runs the selected tests. This will pre-publish the test project to ensure that what is debugged matches what is on the server.
- **Run with Coverage**: Starts a test run and collects code coverage information.

**Test execution**

Tests executed from VSCode do not use an AL test runner and there is no way to specify one. Instead, the isolation level of the tests is determined by the [RequiredTestIsolation](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/properties/devenv-requiredtestisolation-property) property on the test codeunit. If the property is not specified, it will run with `Codeunit` level isolation.

You can choose to run entire test codeunits, or specific tests within those codeunits by selecting them in the Test Explorer.

**Code coverage**

**Note:** We currently do not support full line-based code coverage.

When tests are executed with the `Run with Coverage` profile, a new codelens bar above procedures will be visible. This bar shows the number of tests that cover a specific procedure, as well as their current pass/fail count. Clicking on this codelens will run the tests that cover the specific procedure. This is useful for running the most relevant tests when modifying a specific procedure.

**Agentic test running**

Agents within Visual Studio Code are able to run tests via Visual Studio Code's in-built `runTest` tool. For enabling test-running for other agents, refer to the `ALMCP` server that is part of the `al` dotnet tool package. See [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-tool-package) for more information.

**Disabling test integration**

If you are using a third-party extension for running AL test from VSCode, these new capabilities may conflict with your existing solution. In this case, you can add `al.disableTestRunning: "true"` to your VSCode settings to disable this feature.

entries.body_md:
The [AL dotnet tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-tool-package) now supports a new command: `LaunchMcpServer`. This starts up an HTTP based MCP server which can be used by coding agents to invoke AL-specific development tools. The basic usage is:

`al LaunchMcpServer --projects "C:\Users\MyUser\MyALProject"`

This launches an MCP server, which will track changes within the `MyALProject` folder and provide tools such as the ability to compile the project. In addition to the `projects` parameter, the following parameters can be used to configure the behavior of the MCP server:

```
  --projects                Required. Semicolon-separated list of AL project paths to load.

  --port                    (Default: 5000) Port number for the HTTP server (default: 5000).

  --codeanalyzers           Semicolon-separated list of code analyzers to enable.

  --rulesetpath             Path to the ruleset file.

  --packagecachepath        Semicolon-separated list of package cache directories.

  --assemblyprobingpaths    Semicolon-separated list of assembly probing paths.

  --outfolder               Output folder for compilation artifacts.

  --help                    Display this help screen.

  --version                 Display version information.
```

entries.title: ALTool: Workspace commands
entries.body_md:
The AL command line tool now includes a set of `workspace` commands for working with multi-project AL workspaces. The recommended way to install the tool is via the [Business Central Development Tools NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Dynamics.BusinessCentral.Development.Tools), which is a [.NET tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/global-tools) that provides the `al` command:

```bash
dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.Dynamics.BusinessCentral.Development.Tools
```

##### `workspace create`

Creates a `.code-workspace` file by recursively searching one or more folders for AL projects (folders containing `app.json`). Each discovered project is added to the workspace with its name read from the manifest.

```bash
al workspace create my.code-workspace ./src
```

When the specified folders are themselves AL projects, only those folders are included. Otherwise, the command searches subdirectories recursively and excludes nested projects that fall under another project root.

##### `workspace compile`

Compiles all projects in a workspace in the correct dependency order. The command reads each project's manifest to build a dependency graph, then parallelizes compilations where possible.

```bash
al workspace compile my.code-workspace
```

The following options are available:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--maxcpucount` | Maximum number of concurrent compilations. Defaults to the number of processors. |
| `--packagecachepath` | Semicolon-separated list of package cache directories. |
| `--assemblyprobingpaths` | Semicolon-separated list of assembly probing paths. |
| `--analyzers` | Built-in analyzers to run (CodeCop, AppSourceCop, PTECop, UICop). |
| `--customanalyzers` | Paths to custom analyzer assemblies. Supports absolute paths, paths relative to the workspace directory, and well-known variables (for example, `${AnalyzerFolder}/MyAnalyzer.dll`). |
| `--features` | Features to enable (LcgTranslationFile, TranslationFile, GenerateCaptions). |
| `--generatereportlayout` | Generate report layout. |
| `--define` | Preprocessor symbols to define. |
| `--sourcerepositoryurl` | Source repository URL for the workspace. |
| `--sourcecommit` | Source commit ID for the workspace. |
| `--loglevel` | Logging level. |
| `--logdirectory` | Directory to store compilation log files. |

##### `workspace map`

Generates a Markdown file with a Mermaid dependency diagram from a workspace. The output includes a visual graph of inter-project dependencies, a project details table, and warnings for any circular dependencies detected.

```bash
al workspace map my.code-workspace
al workspace map my.code-workspace output.md
```

entries.title: Quick uptake of namespaces
entries.body_md:
A new code action has been introduced to fix CodeCop rule [AA0247](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/analyzers/codecop-aa0247) by adding namespaces to .al files that are missing them. The namespace is resolved in the following order:

1. Read and parse the newly added `al.namespaceTemplate` setting. The `$(parentfolder)` placeholder can be used to dynamically insert the directory of an AL file.
2. If `namespaceTemplate` is not defined or any part of it does not resolve to a valid identifier name, the system attempts to deduce the namespace from sibling files (AL files in the same folder) by parsing their namespaces and using the longest common part.
3. If there are no sibling files, they don't specify a namespace, or there is no common part, the fallback is `publisher.projectname`.
4. If `publisher.projectname` does not resolve to a valid namespace name, no namespace is added.

ALTool: New "compile" Command Support
entries.body_md:
ALTool now supports invoking `alc` for compiling AL packages. The syntax is:

```
altool compile <alc arguments>
```

This feature is particularly useful when used with the [Business Central Development Tools NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Dynamics.BusinessCentral.Development.Tools). The package is a [.NET tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/global-tools) that includes the AL development tools required for pipelines. Unlike the .vsix installation, it can easily be installed in a pipeline. When installed as a global tool, you can start a compilation by using the following command:

```
AL compile <alc arguments>
```
The `AL` command acts as a convenient alias for ALTool when installed via the NuGet package.

To explore all available commands for ALTool (or AL alias), run the tool without any arguments. Currently supported commands include:

| Command                        | Description                                           |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `compile`                      | Compile a package using `alc.exe`.                   |
| `GetPackageManifest`           | Retrieve the manifest from a `.app` file.            |
| `CreateSymbolPackage`          | Create a symbol-only package from a `.app` file.     |
| `GetLatestSupportedRuntimeVersion` | Get the latest supported AL runtime version for a platform version. |
| `help`                         | Display detailed information about a specific command. |
| `version`                      | Display version information.                         |

This enhancement streamlines the AL development process, especially in CI/CD pipelines, by providing a more accessible and efficient way to compile AL packages.

entries.title: RequiredTestIsolation Property in AL tests
entries.body_md:
We have introduced a new `RequiredTestIsolation` property in test codeunits, which allows engineers to set the required TestIsolation for the test codeunit to run in. If the selected TestRunner does not satisfy the test codeunit's `RequiredTestIsolation` property, then the tests might fail.

The property can be used to group tests for execution and reporting in CI/CD pipelines.

If a test codeunit has `RequiredTestIsolation = None`, then it can run by a TestRunner with any TestIsolation.

If a test codeunit has `RequiredTestIsolation = Codeunit`, then it requires a TestRunner with Codeunit TestIsolation.

If a test codeunit has `RequiredTestIsolation = Function`, then it requires a TestRunner with Function TestIsolation.

If a test codeunit has `RequiredTestIsolation = Disabled`, then it requires a TestRunner with Disabled TestIsolation.

entries.title: Allow deprecating external business events
entries.body_md:
We have added support for deprecating `ExternalBusinessEvent` type events.

The process follows the standard obsoletion steps for procedures with one additional requirement:

Step 1: Mark the event as obsolete pending
 - Decorate the procedure with the `[Obsolete('<Reason>','<Tag>')]` attribute.
 - Prefix the `DisplayName` of the `ExternalBusinessEvent` attribute with an `[OBSOLETE]` marker.

Step 2: Remove the obsolete pending event in an upcoming version

entries.title: Example code
entries.body_md:
```AL
codeunit 10 MyCodeunit
{
    [ExternalBusinessEvent('MyEvent', '[OBSOLETE] MyEventDisplayName', 'Description', EventCategory::MyValue, '1.0')]
    [Obsolete('The event will be replaced by version 2.0 of MyEvent', '27.0')]
    procedure MyEvent()
    begin
    end;

    [ExternalBusinessEvent('MyEvent', 'MyEventDisplayName', 'Description', EventCategory::MyValue, '2.0')]
    procedure MyEvent2()
    begin
    end;
}
```

entries.title: Remarks
entries.body_md:
It is also possible to obsolete the containing object without deprecating the external business event itself. This is because external business events are identified by their (app ID - event name - event version) triplet from the external subscriber's perspective, independent of their containing object or procedure within AL.
In such scenarios, you must relocate the event within the same app while following the standard obsoletion process for the original containing object.

entries.title: Mocking HTTP calls in AL tests
entries.body_md: We have introduced a new handler type `HttpClientHandler` to allow mocking the response of HTTP requests in test codeunits. This feature allows for more controlled and easier testing of modules that interact with external services. The feature is limited to OnPrem instances only.

entries.title: HttpClientHandler
entries.body_md: When an `HttpClientHandler` is added to a test method, every HTTP request that occurs during the execution of that test will be intercepted and routed to the handler. The handler method signature is as follows: it receives a `TestHttpRequestMessage` that contains information about the HTTP request, as well as a `TestHttpResponseMessage` that contains the mocked HTTP response values that should be updated by the handler. The Boolean return value indicates whether to fall through and issue the original HTTP request (true) or to use the mocked response (false).

entries.title: TestHttpRequestPolicy Property
entries.body_md:
We have also introduced a new property on test codeunits called `TestHttpRequestPolicy`. This property determines how outbound HTTP requests are treated during test execution and has the following possible values:

- **BlockOutboundRequests**: Any HTTP request issued during the test execution that is not caught and handled by an HTTP client handler will raise an exception.
- **AllowOutboundFromHandler**: All HTTP requests issued during the test execution are required to be caught by an HTTP client handler. The handler is allowed to explicitly fall through to issue the original request to the external endpoint.
- **AllowAllOutboundRequests**: All outbound HTTP requests issued during the test execution are allowed.

entries.title: Resources in extensions
entries.body_md:
Resource files can now be packaged as part of an extension. To add resources to your extension, the following property has to be set in your app.json:

```JSON
"resourceFolders": [<list of folders that contain resources>]
```

The folders should be listed relative to the root of your project. For example:

```JSON
"resourceFolders": ["Resources"]
```

This will include all files under the folder 'resources'. The resource folders themselves can contain additional subfolders. For example, you could have the following folder structure:

```
MyApp
| - Resources/
  | - Images/
    | - MyImage.png
  | - Configuration/
    | - MyConfiguration.json
| - src/
  | - MyCodeunit.codeunit.al
```

Access to these resources is done through the `NavApp.GetResource("resource name": Text; var instream: Instream; [optional] encoding: TextEncoding)` method. The name of a resource is its path from the root of its resource folder. So for the folder structure above, you can do:

```AL
procedure MyProc()
var
    resultStream: Instream;
    jsonText: Text;
begin
    NavApp.GetResource("Images/MyImage.png", resultStream);
    // Do stuff with the blob in the resultStream object

    NavApp.GetResource("Configuration/MyConfiguration.json", resultStream, TextEncoding::UTF8);
    jsonText := resultStream.Read(jsonText);
end
```

There are also the methods `NavApp.GetResourceAsText("resource name": Text; [optional] encoding: TextEncoding): Text` and `NavApp.GetResourceAsJson("resource name": Text; [optional] encoding: TextEncoding): JsonObject` that directly retrieves resources as `Text` or `JsonObject` types.

The method `NavApp.ListResources([optional] filter: Text)` is also provided to allow for iteration over resources. The `filter` value for the method can contain wildcards. If it does not contain wildcards, then any resources with the filter text within its name will be returned. For example:

```AL
/**
* For the following resource structure:
* Resources/
*     Images/
*         SampleImage1.png
*         SampleImage2.png
*         SampleImage3.jpg
*         TemplateImage.jpg
*     Snippet/
*         SampleSnippet.txt
*         TemplateSnippet.txt
*/

// This will return: ["Images/SampleImage1.png","Images/SampleImage2.png","Images/SampleImage3.jpg", "SampleSnippet.txt"]
NavApp.ListResources("Sample");

// This will return: ["Images/SampleImage1.png","Images/SampleImage2.png"]
NavApp.ListResources("Images/*.png")
```

Resources can only be accessed within the scope of the app that contains them. This means that there is no way to access the resources of another app.

When selected, Visual Studio Code will open and prompt you to clone or open the Git repository for the extension and synchronize it with the commit version used to compile it, using the repo metadata included in the extension. It will also remember the local path where the repository is located for easier access. This feature empowers support, consultants, and developers to navigate code, hotfix builds, or sync to get the latest changes for investigation or development.

entries.title: Type testing and casting operators for interfaces
entries.body_md: In this version, we’ve introduced support for type testing and casting interfaces in the AL language. Two new operators; `is` and `as`, have been added to facilitate these operations.

entries.title: The `is` operator
entries.body_md:
The `is` operator allows you to test whether an instance of an interface or the content of a variant supports a specific interface. Here’s the syntax for using the `is` keyword:


```
procedure TestInterface(intf: Interface IFoo)
begin
    if intf is IBar then
        Message('I also support IBar');
end;
```

You can also use the `is` operator with variants:

```
procedure TestVariant(v: Variant)
begin
    if v is IBar then
        Message('I support IBar');
end;
```

entries.title: The `as` operator
entries.body_md:
The `as` operator is used for casting an instance of an interface to a specific interface. If the source interface does not implement the target interface, it will throw an error at runtime. Here’s an example:

```
procedure CastInterface(intf: Interface IFoo): Interface IBar
begin
    exit(intf as IBar); // Throws an error if 'intf' doesn't implement 'IBar'
end;
```

Similarly, the `as` keyword works with variants:

```
procedure CastInterface(v: Variant): Interface IBar
begin
    exit(v as IBar); // Throws an error if 'v' doesn't implement 'IBar'
end;
```

entries.title: Support for extending interfaces
`This` keyword
entries.body_md:
We have added support for the `this` keyword for self-reference on all objects. The main benefits are

* Allow codeunits to pass a reference to `this` as an argument to another method.
* Improve readability by signaling that a referenced symbol is a member on the object itself.

We have added a CodeCop rule [AA0248](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/analyzers/codecop-aa0248) that is enabled by default with severity 'hidden'. 'Hidden' means that it shows up as three dots in the editor, but not as a diagnostics in the Problem view or in pipelines.
There is also a CodeFixer to add the `this` keyword.

entries.title: Relaxing AppSource affix and ID range validation for apps
entries.body_md:
Affixes no longer need to be added to extension members on apps from the same publisher. Furthermore, table extension fields will be able to use the ID range of the base table, if the base table is from the same publisher. The purpose of affixes and ID ranges is to ensure there are no conflicts between apps from different publishers. With this change, publishers have more flexibility in designing their apps, but will also have to ensure that there are no conflicts
within their own apps. You can see this in detail in our [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-checklist-submission-faq#questions-about-names-affixes-and-id-ranges).

Its purpose is to help the interoperability of AL with various CI/CD integrations which may not support comments in json files, a scenario which leads to failures that are hard to detect and debug. The warning can be suppressed via a ruleset or the `suppressWarnings` property in the manifest file.

entries.title: Support for multiple extensions to same target and extensions and target in same app
entries.body_md:
We have expanded the support for extension objects to help achieve better separation of concerns in large apps. The following changes have been made:

* Extensions can now exist in the same app as their target.
* Multiple extensions to the same target can exist in the same app.

For table extensions in the same app as their target, the fields and keys will be moved to the base table to prevent SQL-joins at runtime.

Since extension objects from a given app are applied on the target following the extension object ID, the following compiler validation was introduced:

* The base object cannot reference members from extension objects.
* Extension objects can reference members from other extension objects in the same app only if the other extension object has a lower object ID.

entries.body_md: AL Table Proxy Generator tool (altpgen) now requires two additional arguments: `ClientId` and `RedirectUri`. entries.title: Script/Css/Image paths on control add-ins can be relative to the control add-in source file.
entries.body_md:
Control add-in resources can also be stored relative to the file containing the control add-in source.

The search order for resources is now:

1. Relative to the project root
2. Relative to the control add-in source.

The following example shows the two options.

file: MyControlAddIn.al
```
controladdin MyControlAddIn
{
    Scripts = './js/myscript.js';
    StyleSheets = 'css/mystyle.css';
    ...
}
```
Resources are relative to project root:
```
.
[src]
    MyControlAddIn.al
[resources]
    [js]
        myscript.js
    [css]
        mystyle.css
app.json
```

Resources are relative to controladdin source:
```
.
[src]
    MyControlAddIn.al
    [resources]
        [js]
            MyScript.js
        [css]
            MyStyle.css
app.json
```

entries.title: Isolated Storage - New method overloads for use with the SecretText type

When values are added as `SecretText`, the runtime will ensure they can only be retrieved in the same type. This makes it possible to ensure that they are protected from debugging throughout their entire lifetime. In addition, a new overload to the `Contains` method was added to allow checking if a value was added as a `SecretText`.

```
{
}
```
by including a markdown file with the following content
```
---
uid: O:Enum::MyNS#MyEnum
summary: This is my new comment
---
```

entries.title: Introducing Namespaces: A New Way to Organize Your AL Code
entries.body_md: We are excited to announce that AL for Business Central now supports namespaces. Namespaces are similar to other code languages, and they allow you to group your objects and code in a logical and hierarchical way. With namespaces, you can avoid naming conflicts between different extensions, and make your code easier to maintain and understand. You can also see the relationship between different objects at a glance, and use the dot notation to access them. For example, you can use `MyNamespace.MyTable` to refer to a table object in your namespace. Namespaces are optional, but we highly recommend using them to improve your coding experience and productivity. To learn more about how to use namespaces in AL, please check out our documentation here [Namespaces in AL](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-namespaces-overview?wt.mc_id=d365bc_inproduct_alextension)

entries.title: Open Visual Studio Code from web client
entries.body_md: This feature simplifies the process of setting up Visual Studio Code environments for investigation and troubleshooting by allowing one-click access from the web client, available in both from the **Page Inspection** and **Help & Support** pages. You can choose to create a new project or update an existing one, which is configured to match your running instance, including launch configurations and dependencies in the app.json file. Users can download required symbols, easily navigate to source definitions, and seamlessly attach to the current session for regular and snapshot debugging, eliminating manual setup efforts. For more information, see [Troubleshoot in Visual Studio Code directly from the web client](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-troubleshoot-vscode-webclient?wt.mc_id=d365bc_inproduct_alextension).

entries.title: Introducing ALDoc: a new command line tool for generating reference documentation for AL extensions
entries.body_md: ALDoc works with DocFx to create a static website that contains detailed information about the objects, methods, properties, and events in one or more .app files. You can use ALDoc to document your own extensions or explore the APIs of other extensions. To learn more about how to use ALDoc, visit [Generating help with the ALDoc tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/help/help-aldoc-generate-help?wt.mc_id=d365bc_inproduct_alextension)

Added report property ExcelLayoutMultipleDataSheets
entries.body_md:
Added a new Boolean report property [ExcelLayoutMultipleDataSheets](https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/properties/devenv-ExcelLayoutMultipleDataSheets-property?wt.mc_id=d365bc_inproduct_alextension) that controls how Excel data sheets are created when using an Excel layout.
Use this property to emit root data items to separate Excel sheets or to a single sheet named Data.
Multiple sheets will be named #DataItemName, where DataItemName is the dataitem name used in the report design. Adding new empty Excel layouts to the report will use the property value to determine the sheet structure.

The default is to use a single sheet for all data.
